newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Century Zinc says Aboriginal groups sign mine pact.
newsitem.headline: Century Zinc says Aboriginal groups sign mine pact.

text.p: Australian aboriginal groups who have been in dispute over development of the A$1 billion Century zinc mine in the state of Queensland had now agreed with RTZ Corp Plc-CRA Ltd to its development, Century Zinc Ltd said on Thursday.
"At the end of last night all twelve had signed. We are prepared to make our A$60 million package available," a spokesman for RTZ-CRA subsidiary, Century Zinc, told Reuters.

Talks on the mine's development collapsed in February following failure by the parties to obtain signatures of 12 Aboriginal groups who were claiming land rights on areas surrounding the mine in the northwest of the state.
Century Zinc had offered the Aboriginal groups a A$60 million aid package.
The fate of an earlier A$30 million Queensland state government aid package to aboriginals as part of the negotiating procedure was unknown at this stage, the spokesman said.
"The state has yet to put its A$30 million package back on the table," he said.
The signatures to the agreement were obtained after meetings in northwest Queensland between Aboriginal groups including members of the Waanyi tribe who had earlier withdrawn their approval.

In January, Pasminco Ltd said it would buy the Century mine and nearby Dugald River zinc projects from RTZ-CRA for A$345 million, conditional on the Queensland state government issuing mine leases which depended on Aboriginal groups resolving the impasse over land tenure.

Pasminco, the world's biggest zinc producer, had earlier planned to buy half of the mine's annual output of 780,000 tonnes of low iron-bearing concentrates to feed its Budel zinc smelter in the Netherlands.
It later agreed to purchase the project, pending claim-free title to the site and access to land covering a slurry pipeline leading to a port on the Gulf of Carpentaria coast.
Century's development is crucial to the continued operation of the Budel smelter, whose current operating licence requires it to cease generating hazardous jarosite zinc residue.
If development work was to start on the mine in the next few months, production could commence in the latter part of the year 2000, Century Zinc has said.
Pasminco said the collapse of talks in February were potentially damaging, but it could still meet its deadline if things progressed within the six months from that month.
The companies and aboriginal groups were scheduled to move to the Federal Native Title Tribunal in an arbitration process next Monday in the northwest mining city of Mt Isa.
